info.name: interceptor
info.description:
interceptor endpoints, called through the LiteLLM pass-through registered in ai/litellm/litellm_config.yaml (`pass_through_endpoints` → `/v1/interceptor` → `http://interceptor:8080`, `include_subpath: true`, methods GET/POST/DELETE, `forward_headers: true` — so `multipart/form-data` uploads for /profiles/{name}/refresh forward correctly). Every request is authenticated with a Bearer token from a LiteLLM virtual key. Set the collection variables `litellm` (e.g. http://localhost:4001) and `virtual master key` (an sk-… key issued from the LiteLLM Admin UI → Virtual Keys) — every request inherits them via collection-level auth. See ai/interceptor/INTERCEPTOR.md for the full endpoint reference and ai/litellm/LITELLM.md for issuing virtual keys.

Reaching the service: the container has NO `ports:` mapping (INTERCEPTOR.md § Reaching the service). Port 8080 is reachable only from inside `ai_shared`. Options: (1) another `ai_shared` container via `http://interceptor:8080/...`, (2) your host via the LiteLLM pass-through `{{litellm}}/v1/interceptor/...` (what this collection uses), (3) `docker exec interceptor curl ...`. `http://localhost:8080` from the host does NOT reach the container — if something answers there it's a separate bare-metal `python app.py` run against the host's `/data/profiles` (used during profile capture with a visible display).

MCP: LiteLLM ALSO advertises the interceptor as an MCP server via `mcp_servers.interceptor` (url `http://interceptor:8080/mcp`) — models see the four tools (capture_url, list_profiles, list_jobs, get_job) through that path. The MCP requests below are useful for debugging the transport directly.

Actions: POST /capture also takes `page_script` / `actions` / `stop_when_matched` to fill inputs and click buttons (through shadow DOM) so the page fires the request you want — see `POST /capture (actions)` and INTERCEPTOR.md § Page scripts and actions.

Screenshots: a screenshot is an `actions` step, `{"type": "screenshot", "scale": 0.5}`, that can sit anywhere in the list (max 10 per request). Each image comes back base64 on its own step in `actions_report.actions[i].value`; capture_url on MCP delivers each as a labelled ImageContent block instead. With no `url_patterns` (allowed only when an action is a screenshot) the capture ends as soon as the actions finish. `click` / `fill` scroll their element to the centre of the viewport, so a `{"type": "scroll", "to": "top"}` (or `"selector": …`) step right before a screenshot frames it. See `POST /capture (screenshots between actions)` and INTERCEPTOR.md § Screenshots.

Viewing screenshots: a collection-level post-response script renders every screenshot step in `actions_report` from POST /capture, in step order — open the **Visualize** tab in the response pane after sending. Each image's header says which step took it, what ran just before it, and `page_url` (where the tab was at that step); a failed screenshot step shows its error instead.

**Error bodies.** Each endpoint's `#### Schemas` section -- at the end of its first request's description, generated from `interceptor.schemas.json` by `scripts/api_schemas.py render` -- documents its request body, its success response and every error status whose body is more than FastAPI's `{"detail": "<message>"}`. Any other error answers that `{"detail": "<message>"}`; a request that fails FastAPI's own validation answers 422 `{"detail": [{"type", "loc", "msg", "input", ...}]}`, one entry per problem. A request sent through LiteLLM (`{{litellm}}`) can also be refused by LiteLLM itself before it reaches the service -- 401 / 403 for a missing or unauthorised key -- with LiteLLM's `{"error": {"message", "type", "param", "code"}}`.

exec: // Renders every screenshot step in actions_report from POST /capture in the
// Visualize tab of the response pane, in step order. A no-op for every other
// response (MCP results carry each image as an ImageContent block, not base64 here).
try { body = pm.response.json(); } catch (e) { /* not JSON */ }
ok: ok, error: r.error || 'no image', mime: v.mime_type, data: v.data_base64

variable.description: LiteLLM base URL. Localhost publish is 4001 (PORT_LITELLM); on ai_shared it's http://litellm:4000; behind cloudflared it's https://your-litellm-host.

LiteLLM virtual key (Admin UI → Virtual Keys, or /key/generate API). The pass-through runs with `auth: true`, so a non-admin virtual key needs `/v1/interceptor` in its (or its team's) `metadata.allowed_passthrough_routes` — set under `metadata`, by a proxy admin, because the top-level field is Enterprise-only; the master key works without it. Otherwise 403. See ai/litellm/LITELLM.md § Pass-through auth. Sent as `Authorization: Bearer {{virtual master key}}` by the collection-level auth.

Named Chrome profile. Must match `[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}` (profiles.py:_NAME_RE). Used by GET /profiles/{name}, POST /profiles/{name}/refresh, DELETE /profiles/{name}. Discover valid values via GET /profiles.

12-char hex job_id returned by POST /capture (or listed by GET /jobs). Fill in to run GET /jobs/{job_id} and POST /jobs/{job_id}/cancel. Completed captures are NOT retained — the id is only valid while the capture is in flight.

MCP transport session id — paste the `mcp-session-id` response header value returned by the `MCP — initialize` request. Subsequent MCP calls need it. This is FastMCP's HTTP-transport session cookie, unrelated to any interceptor job_id.

formdata.description: Required. A .tgz/.tar.gz of a captured Chrome --user-data-dir. The endpoint uses tarfile.open(mode='r:*') so gzip/bzip2/xz auto-detect. Field name MUST be exactly `archive` — any other name returns 422 with no unpack performed. Archive the CONTENTS of the profile dir (`tar czf x.tgz -C <profile_dir> .`), not the dir itself.

{
  "url": "https://example.com/dashboard",
  "url_patterns": ["example\\.com/api/v1/items", "example\\.com/api/v1/user"],
  "profile": "{{profileName}}",
  "capture_window_seconds": 20,
  "keep_open": false,
  "login_timeout": 300,
  "max_matches_per_pattern": null,
  "debug_logging": false,
  "login_url_patterns": ["login", "signin", "/auth"],
  "page_script": null,
  "actions": [],
  "actions_ready_timeout_seconds": null,
  "stop_when_matched": false,
  "login_actions": [],
  "login_actions_timeout_seconds": null
}

{
  "url": "https://support.enphase.com/feoc-compliance/",
  "url_patterns": ["webruntime/api/apex/execute"],
  "profile": "{{profileName}}",
  "capture_window_seconds": 60,
  "login_timeout": 30,
  "login_url_patterns": ["login", "signin", "/auth", "sso\\.enphaseenergy\\.com"],
  "stop_when_matched": true,
  "actions_ready_timeout_seconds": 60,
  "page_script": null,
  "actions": [
    {"type": "fill", "selector": "textarea[placeholder='Serial number']", "value": "532614044013"},
    {"type": "evaluate", "script": "(() => { window.__ciN0 = (window._capturedResponses || []).length; return window.__ciN0; })()"},
    {"type": "click", "selector": "button[type=submit]", "text": "Submit"},
    {"type": "evaluate", "script": "(async () => { const until = Date.now() + 30000; while (Date.now() < until) { const c = (window._capturedResponses || []).slice(window.__ciN0 || 0).filter(x => /webruntime\\/api\\/apex\\/execute/.test(x.url)); if (c.length) return {new_apex_responses: c.length}; await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 250)); } throw new Error('no new apex/execute response within 30s of Submit'); })()", "timeout_s": 35},
    {"type": "wait", "seconds": 2},
    {"type": "screenshot", "format": "jpeg", "scale": 0.5}
  ]
}

request.description:
Same endpoint as POST /capture, driving the page first: for pages that only fire the request you want after someone fills a form and clicks a button. The page's OWN code sends the request (so CSRF-signed APIs such as Salesforce LWR's `webruntime/api/apex/execute` work — a hand-written fetch() from page_script gets 401), and the response arrives in `matches` through the normal capture path. The body is the verified Enphase FEOC serial lookup (2026-10-02); for another site, discover the selectors first with a `page_script` (INTERCEPTOR.md § Worked example). The result is the match whose `returnValue` is a JSON string of an array, e.g. `[{"sn":"532614044013","feoc":"Yes","sku":"IQ8HC-72-M-DOM-US",...}]`.

Order: Chrome launches → readiness gate (tab off about:blank, not on a `login_url_patterns` URL, document.readyState complete, interceptor.js hook installed; up to `actions_ready_timeout_seconds`, default capture_window_seconds) → `page_script` (an EXPRESSION — use an async IIFE for several statements; its value comes back as actions_report.page_script.value) → each action in order, stopping at the first failure (the rest are reported `skipped`) — except a failed `screenshot` step, which is recorded and the run continues.

Step types: `wait_for` {selector, text?, state?: visible|attached, timeout_s?}; `fill` {selector, value, text?, clear?: true, timeout_s?} — focuses the real <input>/<textarea> (descending from a component host such as lightning-input into its shadow root), types with trusted Input.insertText, fires change, blurs; `click` {selector, text?, method?: mouse|js, timeout_s?} — trusted mouse press/release at the element's centre; `press` {key, selector?, text?, timeout_s?} — Enter/Tab/Escape/Backspace/Delete/Space/arrows/Home/End/PageUp/PageDown or one character; `select` {selector, value, text?, timeout_s?} — native <select> only; `wait` {seconds}; `evaluate` {script, timeout_s?}; `screenshot` {format?: jpeg|png|webp, quality?: 1-100, full_page?, scale?: 0<s<=2, max_height?: 100-16384, timeout_s?: 30} — an image of the page at that point (the trailing one in this body shows the result the lookup rendered; see `POST /capture (screenshots between actions)`); `scroll` {selector?, text?, to?: top|bottom, by?: px (negative is up), block?: start|center|end|nearest (selector-only form), timeout_s?} — at least one of selector / to / by, to and by exclusive: frames an element at the top of the viewport, or jumps / nudges the container that actually scrolls (the document, or the largest visible inner overflow-y:auto element when the document doesn't — Salesforce Lightning — or, with a selector, that element's scroll container); value {target, element?, scroll_top, scroll_height, client_height, at_bottom}, nothing to scroll is a no-op (target null). `timeout_s` defaults to 15 (30 for screenshot; for scroll it bounds only the element lookup). Selectors are CSS matched in the document and inside every open shadow root, each tree separately (a descendant combinator never crosses a shadow boundary — `lightning-input input` matches nothing; use `lightning-input` or `input[name=…]`); `text` filters by visible text / value / aria-label / placeholder / title (substring, or /regex/flags); the first visible match wins.

`stop_when_matched: true` ends the window once every url_patterns bucket has a match AND the actions have finished — the page makes three Apex calls on load (same URL), so the two `evaluate` steps hold the window open: the first records how many responses interceptor.js has captured, the second waits for a new Apex one after Submit; the trailing `wait` lets it reach the service before the window closes, and the closing `screenshot` step shows the page as the lookup left it (open the Visualize tab). Cleanup still runs.

Response: the usual CaptureResponse plus `actions_report` {page_script: ActionResult|null, actions: [{index, type, ok, elapsed_ms, error, value}], aborted_reason: null | 'not ready: …' | 'cancelled' | 'actions[i] (type) failed: …' | 'capture window ended before actions finished'} and `ended_early`. GET /jobs shows phase `actions` and metadata.actions_done / actions_total while the steps run.

Errors: as POST /capture — 422 for an unknown action `type`, a missing field, or a `scroll` that mixes its forms (no selector/to/by, to with by, block with to/by, text without selector), 400 `invalid action: …` for an unknown press key, 422 when `stop_when_matched` has no url_patterns — all before a port is taken. See INTERCEPTOR.md § Page scripts and actions.

#### Schemas

See *POST /capture*, the first request of this endpoint.

request.description:
Same endpoint as POST /capture (actions), plus automatic login: the verified Enphase FEOC serial lookup with `login_actions` that sign the profile back in when its SSO session has expired, instead of returning `login_wall: true` until someone re-uploads the profile. Needs `ai/interceptor/logins/<profile>.json` (checked in; bind-mounted read-only at INTERCEPTOR_LOGINS_DIR=/config/logins, re-read per request): {"allowed_origins": ["https://sso.enphaseenergy.com"], "values": {"username": "${ENV:INTERCEPTOR_LOGIN_ENPHASE_USERNAME}", "password": "${ENV:INTERCEPTOR_LOGIN_ENPHASE_PASSWORD}"}} — every value is an environment reference; the credentials themselves are set in .env and passed through the interceptor compose `environment:` block (an unset one is a 400 naming the variable). GET /profiles shows which reference names (`login_keys`) a profile has.

`login_actions` run ONLY if the tab lands on a URL matching `login_url_patterns`, once per capture, never retried (a wrong password can't lock the account by looping). Steps: wait_for / fill / click / press / select / wait / scroll (it reads nothing; for a sign-in button below the fold) — NO evaluate and NO screenshot (422; an image of the login form would carry the username into the response). `${key}` is resolved from the file's `values` ONLY in a fill `value` (`$$` = a literal $); a `${` in any other field is a 400. In the regular `actions`, `${…}` is plain text. Every fill first checks the tab's `location.origin` against the file's `allowed_origins` (again right before typing) and fails with `origin <o> not allowed for this fill` otherwise. The login steps use their own gate (real URL + document complete; login URLs allowed, no capture hook needed). When they finish, the session's usual wait sees the tab leave the login page and re-navigates to `url`; the serial-number `actions` (whose gate has been waiting out the login) then run as usual. `login_actions_timeout_seconds` (1-600, default 60) caps the login run; `capture_window_seconds` must cover the login, the SSO redirect and the target page load (~120 s). The login selectors were read off the live SSO form (sso.enphaseenergy.com/login: one page, #username, #password, input[type=submit].button "Log in"); a failed step's error names the one that missed if Enphase changes it.

The request (and so every log line, GET /jobs record and 422 echo) only ever carries `${password}`; the secret goes only into the in-memory steps handed to the browser. Response: the usual CaptureResponse plus `login_actions_report` — same shape as `actions_report`, steps named `login_actions[i]`, a fill reports {element, value_length} only; null unless login_actions were sent AND a login wall was hit (so null on the next run means the session the fast path persisted is still good). `login_wall` is true only if still on the login page at the end. The job log gets one line: `login_actions ok=<bool> failed_at=<index/type>`.

Errors (all before a port is taken): 400 no logins file for the profile, 400 unknown `${key}` (the message lists the defined names, never values), 400 `allowed_origins` missing/empty/not an origin, 400 `${` outside a fill value or a malformed reference, 400 `invalid login_actions: …` (e.g. unknown press key), 422 an `evaluate` or `screenshot` step or a malformed step, 422 `login_actions` with empty `login_url_patterns`. See INTERCEPTOR.md § Login actions.

#### Schemas

See *POST /capture*, the first request of this endpoint.

Screenshots are an `actions` step: `{"type": "screenshot", "format"?: "jpeg"|"png"|"webp", "quality"?: 1-100 (80), "full_page"?: false, "scale"?: 0<s<=2 (1.0), "max_height"?: 100-16384 (8000), "timeout_s"?: 30}`. Put one anywhere in `actions` — after a click to see what it did, between a fill and the submit, at the end — up to 10 per request (an 11th is a 422). Each image comes back on its own step: `actions_report.actions[i].value` = {format, mime_type, width, height, full_page, bytes, page_url, data_base64}, where `page_url` is where the tab was at that step. Open the **Visualize** tab to see every image in step order, each headed `actions[i] screenshot — after actions[i-1] (<type>) — <page_url>, WxH, KB`.

This body is screenshot-only: no `url_patterns` (allowed ONLY when an action is a screenshot), so the window ends as soon as the actions finish — `ended_early: true`, a response in seconds rather than after `capture_window_seconds`, which stays the upper bound. The smallest form is `{"url": "https://example.com", "profile": "{{profileName}}", "actions": [{"type": "screenshot"}]}`. `status: 'loading'` is NORMAL for a page that fires no JSON XHRs — judge each shot by its step's `ok` / `error`.

Screenshots between real steps — the Enphase FEOC lookup, seeing the filled form and then the result: `"url_patterns": ["webruntime/api/apex/execute"], "actions": [{"type": "fill", "selector": "textarea[placeholder='Serial number']", "value": "532614044013"}, {"type": "screenshot", "scale": 0.5}, {"type": "click", "selector": "button[type=submit]", "text": "Submit"}, {"type": "wait", "seconds": 5}, {"type": "screenshot", "full_page": true, "scale": 0.5}]` (INTERCEPTOR.md § Screenshots, worked example).

Framing: a viewport screenshot shows wherever the page is scrolled, and `click` / `fill` scroll their element to the CENTRE of the viewport — so put a `scroll` step right before a screenshot to frame it. `{"type": "scroll", "to": "top"}` (this body's `actions[2]`) jumps the page's main scroller to the top: the document, or — when the document doesn't scroll (Salesforce Lightning) — the largest visible inner `overflow-y: auto` element, shadow DOM included. `"to": "bottom"` and `"by": <px>` (negative is up) use the same container; `{"type": "scroll", "selector": "h2", "text": "Results"}` puts that element at the top of the frame (`block`: start|center|end|nearest, default start), and a `selector` with `to` / `by` scrolls that element's own scroll container. The step's `value` is {target: 'window' | '<div class=…>' | null, element?, scroll_top, scroll_height, client_height, at_bottom}; nothing to scroll is a no-op (`target: null`), not a failure. A `full_page` capture always starts at the document's top; the scroll there matters for an inner scroller, whose position the capture keeps. Scroll is allowed in `login_actions`; screenshot is not.

Behaviour: each screenshot settles first (best-effort, ~5 s — covers a step right after a click that navigated) and then shoots the page whether or not it got there. A FAILED screenshot is recorded (`ok: false` + `error`) and the run continues — every other step type stops the run on failure; cancellation and the window ending still stop it. The readiness gate still applies before the first step, so a tab on a login wall gets no image (the step is `skipped`, `login_wall: true`) — send `login_url_patterns: []` to see the login page itself, or `login_actions` to get past it. Not allowed in `login_actions` (422). jpeg viewport ~100-300 KB, `scale: 0.5` ~30-80 KB; base64 in the JSON adds a third. Same port-pool slot / GET /jobs (phase `actions`) / cancel accounting as any capture.

Errors: 422 empty `url_patterns` with no screenshot step, 422 more than 10 screenshot steps, 422 an out-of-range option (scale > 2, quality 0, max_height < 100, unknown format or field), 400 bad profile name or regex, 429 port pool exhausted, 500 Chrome not found. On MCP the same steps go in capture_url's `actions`, and each image arrives as a labelled ImageContent block. See INTERCEPTOR.md § Screenshots.

#### Schemas

See *POST /capture*, the first request of this endpoint.

Signal an in-flight capture to wake early, quit Chrome, run cleanup, and return. Operator-only — deliberately NOT exposed on MCP (an LLM can't coordinate cross-agent cancellation). The `POST /capture` caller then receives a normal CaptureResponse with `status="cancelled"` plus any partial matches/captured_urls collected before the abort. Returns {job_id, cancelled: true, was_phase}.

Also the way to reclaim a hung `keep_open=true` slot — cancel bypasses the skip-cleanup path and always terminates Chrome + releases the port + drops the profile-lock (fast path) or temp dir (slow path).

Errors: 404 if the job is unknown or already completed, 409 if the job is already in `cleaning_up` phase (the finally block is running — too late to cancel). See INTERCEPTOR.md § Cancelling a stuck or long-running capture.

#### Schemas

The POST /capture caller then gets a normal response with `status: "cancelled"`. 404 an id not in flight; 409 a capture already in `cleaning_up`.

Response `200` (`application/json`):

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "required": ["job_id", "cancelled", "was_phase"],
  "properties": {
    "job_id": {"type": "string"},
    "cancelled": {"const": true},
    "was_phase": {
      "enum": ["cloning", "capturing", "actions"],
      "description": "The phase the capture was in when the cancel landed"
    }
  }
}
```

item.name: MCP
item.description:
FastMCP JSON-RPC over HTTP forwarded through the LiteLLM pass-through. Note that LiteLLM ALSO advertises the interceptor as an MCP server via `mcp_servers.interceptor` (url `http://interceptor:8080/mcp`) in litellm_config.yaml — models see the tools through that path, not this one. The requests below are useful for debugging the transport directly. Every MCP request MUST use trailing-slash (POST /mcp/), MUST send `Accept: application/json, text/event-stream`, and MUST start with an `initialize` call — copy the `mcp-session-id` response header into the `mcpSessionId` collection variable for subsequent calls.

Four tools are exposed: capture_url, list_profiles, list_jobs, get_job. The `keep_open` and `debug_logging` knobs from POST /capture are deliberately omitted — both are operator-only debug flags. MCP tools NEVER raise — errors surface inside the payload (e.g. `status="error"` with an `error` field, or `{"error": "no active job ..."}`). capture_url returns a TextContent JSON block followed, for every screenshot action that produced an image (in step order), by a TextContent label (`actions[i] screenshot — <page_url>, WxH`) and an ImageContent block carrying the image itself (the JSON keeps only each step's metadata — no base64 duplicated into the text).
